what: POOL-AFFINITY (2026-10-24): the tensor pool deals each job's tasks in contiguous blocks, one a worker -- worker w's block of n tasks over W workers from n/W*w + min(w, n%W) -- each block's counter on a 64-byte line of its own where the compiler has atomics, a worker claiming its block's tasks in ascending order and then the other blocks' leftovers; a job's head leading tasks (a pair or group job's led weight adjoints, every task of a job with no more tasks than workers) claimed in turn first; every value as it was. The records measure the tree after against the tree before on this host, the design a part at a time, and NEXT-0's survey that placed the slice (survey.json: the step a part at a time, the forward's phases and kernels, the pool's cost, the elementwise jobs cold, and six levers measured and not taken)
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz, 4 vCPU (AVX-512F, AMX), 2 MiB of L2 a core, 260 MiB of L3; Linux 6.18; clang 18.1.3 and GCC 13.3 (-std=c11 -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno -pthread; the study's overlays with GCC, as the study builds them); Python 3.11.15, NumPy 2.2.6, torch 2.13.0+cu130 (CPU); OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE
